title: Brain-wave driven wheelchair for paralysis patients using EEG and ML
summary: VIT reports EEG-model development using data from ten people and plans hospital testing of a brain-controlled wheelchair.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Researchers trained models using EEG data from ten people and describe promising tests. Hospital agreements are intended to support further evaluation. The wheelchair aims to improve mobility independence for people with paralysis, but measured mobility changes and sustained patient use remain unreported.
purpose: Enable wheelchair control through brain-signal interpretation.
system: Brain-wave driven wheelchair for paralysis patients using EEG and ML

ratings.reason: EEG training and promising tests are reported. Mobility and independence improvements remain unquantified.

ai_role.statement: The account does not isolate AI’s contribution from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025). Project-submitted account, current as of June 2025. ITU provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 24: Brain-wave driven wheelchair for paralysis patients using EEG and ML

produced_by: The account does not establish conditions sufficient to reproduce the benefit.
must_hold: The account does not establish requirements for reproducing the benefit in other settings.

headline: EEG wheelchair controls seek greater mobility independence
claim_basis: Sources: the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
